article.headline: Intuit Sinks 9.4% Premarket After Cutting Revenue Outlook, Selling Mailchimp
article.deck: The 12-week cup's buy point is 373.08, and Thursday's close sat 16.9% below it before a premarket drop that pushes the stock further away.
body: Intuit traded at 281.00 at 8:50 a.m. Eastern, down 29.02 or 9.4% from Thursday's close, after headlines said it lowered its fiscal 2027 revenue outlook and agreed to sell Mailchimp. The stock closed Thursday at 310.02, off 3.22 or 1.0%, on volume 1.34x its 50-day average. It sits in a 12-week cup, 29.7% deep, with a buy point of 373.08 and a buy range to 391.73. Thursday's close was 16.9% below the buy point. The cup formed after a much bigger correction, and the stock remains far below its 721.54 high from August 2025.

Nothing on this chart is buyable. Thursday's close sat 54.6% under the 52-week high of 682.27, 2.5% below the 50-day line at 317.91 and 10.9% below the 200-day at 347.87. It was 1.02 ATRs from the 21-day line at 331.57, on the underside. The early entry at the handle high of 351.49 from Nov. 16 is out of reach. Intuit is RS rank 25 of 99 on the desk's list, and the shares are down 53.2% this year and 52.3% over 12 months.

In the quarter ended July 31, earnings per share came to 1.34, down 0.7% from a year earlier, on revenue of $4.354 billion, up 13.7%. The table carries no year-over-year comparison for the earlier quarters. Nov. 19 was the listed earnings date; the figures from that report are not in the desk's data. Intuit has a market value of $82.85 billion and trades at 11.5 times forward earnings.

A Stocktwits headline said the stock drew multiple price target cuts after Intuit lowered its fiscal 2027 revenue outlook. Euronews reported that Bending Spoons will buy Mailchimp from Intuit in a $3.68 billion deal, and GuruFocus described the buyer as Berkshire-backed.
A move back over the 50-day line would be the first repair; until then this is a stock in a downtrend inside a base.
article.watch: Whether the stock holds the base's 262.32 low and the 52-week low of 252.84 from June 22.

article.headline: Ross Stores Drops 5.7% Premarket On Weak Fourth-Quarter Outlook
article.deck: The flat base's buy point is 257.10, 14.5% above Thursday's close, and the premarket price sits under the base's low.
body: Ross Stores traded at 207.26 at 8:50 a.m. Eastern, down 12.62 or 5.7%, after reporting third-quarter results and a fourth-quarter outlook that headlines called weak. The stock closed Thursday at 219.88, off 7.76 or 3.4%, on volume 1.45x its 50-day average. It sits in a 15-week flat base, 15.0% deep, with a buy point of 257.10 and a buy range to 269.96. Thursday's close was 14.5% below the buy point, and the premarket price is under the base's low of 218.43, set Thursday. A flat base that breaks its own low is no longer a flat base.

Thursday's close was 14.4% under the 52-week high of 257.00, 4.9% below the 50-day line at 231.25 and 2.5% below the 200-day at 225.42. It was 0.35 ATRs from the 21-day line at 230.64, on the underside. The early entry at the handle high of 243.87 from Nov. 12 is gone. Ross is RS rank 65 of 99 on the desk's list, up 22.1% this year and 37.5% over 12 months.

The latest quarter in the table, ended July 31, showed earnings per share of 2.66, up 70.5%, on revenue of $6.265 billion, up 13.3%. EPS ran 1.58, 2.00, 2.02 and 2.66 across the four quarters given. The company has a market value of $70.53 billion and a forward P/E of 24.4.

Investing.com reported that Ross tumbled on a weak fourth-quarter earnings outlook. A GuruFocus headline on the earnings call cited 8% comparable sales growth, and an InvestorsHub headline asked why the stock was falling despite strong third-quarter earnings.
article.watch: Whether the stock can retake the 200-day line at 225.42 after opening below the base.

article.headline: Sandisk Falls 6.8% Premarket As Nasdaq Futures Slide After Anthropic Reversal
article.deck: A 21-week deep cup puts the buy point at 294.40, 67.9% above Thursday's close; the stock is in a steep correction, not a setup.
body: Sandisk traded at 88.00 at 8:50 a.m. Eastern, down 6.39 or 6.8%, as Nasdaq 100 futures fell 2.1% and Stocktwits named the stock among names in focus while Anthropic shares reversed their IPO gains. Sandisk closed Thursday at 94.39, off 2.63 or 2.7%, on volume 1.46x its 50-day average. The desk's data shows a 21-week deep cup, 68.2% deep, with a buy point of 294.40 and a buy range to 309.12. Thursday's close was 67.9% below the buy point, and the premarket price is under the base's low of 93.67 from Nov. 17.

Barron's ran a headline Friday reading "Sandisk Stock Looked Like It Fell 87%. Here's What Really Happened." Readers should check the chart's scale against that report; the figures here are as the desk's price data gives them.

On those figures the trend is broken. Thursday's close was 67.9% off the 52-week high of 294.30, 44.7% below the 50-day line at 170.69 and 41.3% below the 200-day at 160.69. It sat 25.1% under the 21-day line at 125.98, 1.62 ATRs away on the underside. The stock fell 45.2% over the past month and 52.7% over three months, though it is still up 218.1% this year. Sandisk is RS rank 93 of 99 on the desk's list.

The quarter ended Sept. 30 showed earnings per share up 6913.3% from a year earlier on revenue of $11.031 billion, up 377.9%. Revenue climbed from $3.025 billion to $5.95 billion, $8.965 billion and $11.031 billion across the four quarters given. The forward P/E is 20.9.
A 24/7 Wall St. headline argued Sandisk has a cleaner setup than SK Hynix through the end of 2026.
article.watch: Whether the stock can stop falling and build a base under the 21-day line at 125.98.
